title: This IVY League University Is Trying to Cancel Change My Mind
description:
Change My Mind was always meant to challenge institutions that fail the people they’re supposed to teach.

The debate topic between myself and Prof. Zimmerman set for this week’s CMM is free speech, where it stands, and who is trying to kill it.

Well, we have our answer. Where the Left thrives, free speech dies.

UPenn is now trying to control the narrative. They’ve told us they will deny our ability to livestream the event. Why? I think we all know the answer.

Regardless, we’ll be there Friday, April 10th, 7 PM ET. LIVESTREAMING. See you then.

comments.text:
Did they not enter into an enforceable contract with you? There was offer and acceptance, then billing/payment for consideration. They indicated that livestreaming was part of the agreement. They cannot unilaterally update the contract or cancel without penalty. They don't get to renegotiate terms after acceptance. I am not a lawyer, so if I'm wrong I'm sure the internet will correct me. But if the university does not honor the terms of your agreement, you are well within your right to sue them for the total value of the contract, including damages to include loss of revenue from ticket/merch sales. Given that this is a public university, you could also sue for a free speech violation alongside the breach of contract.

Left-wing or right-wing, public institutions don't get to restrict speech or breach their contracts. Those that do ought not to receive another taxpayer dime.
